methodology: Both the original research topic and the generated technical specifications were decomposed into atomic information units. Each unit represents a distinct requirement, feature, behavior, or constraint of the water reservoir system. The decomposition focused on identifying independent and self-contained elements that are technically specific and unambiguous. For the original research topic, the decomposition extracted explicit requirements about sensor placement, flow rate control based on water level, and the reset functionality. For the generated technical specifications, the decomposition focused on the module interface, combinational logic functions, input/output signals, water level decoding, nominal flow rate logic, supplemental flow rate logic, and timing considerations. The goal was to create sets of atomic units that could be compared to assess the coverage and similarity between the original topic and the generated specifications.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Three active-high sensors (s[1], s[2], s[3]) are placed vertically at 5-inch intervals.
Water level above s[3] (s[1], s[2], s[3] high): all flow valves closed (fr1, fr2, fr3, dfr low).
Water level between s[3] and s[2] (s[1], s[2] high): only fr1 asserted.
Water level between s[2] and s[1] (s[1] high): fr1 and fr2 asserted.
Water level below s[1] (no sensors high): fr1, fr2, and fr3 asserted.
If the water level increases, dfr is also asserted.
If the water level decreases, dfr is deasserted.
Active-high synchronous reset sets the system to the state where no sensors are asserted.
All flow rate outputs (fr1, fr2, fr3, dfr) are asserted after reset.
The system controls water level using nominal flow valves (fr1, fr2, fr3) and a supplemental flow valve (dfr).
Module has flow rate outputs fr3, fr2, fr1, dfr.
spec_atomic_units: Module interface: input clk, input reset, input [3:1] s, output reg fr3, output reg fr2, output reg fr1, output reg dfr.
Sensor inputs s[3:1] are decoded to determine the current water level.
Nominal flow rates (fr3, fr2, fr1) are determined based on the decoded water level.
Between s[2] and s[1] (s[1] & ~s[2]): fr1 = 1, fr2 = 1, fr3 = 0.
Supplemental flow rate (dfr) is asserted if the previous water level was lower than the current water level.
previous_state[3:0]: A 4-bit input representing the previous water level.
Water Level Decoding: Level_Above_s3 = s[1] & s[2] & s[3]
Water Level Decoding: Level_Between_s3_s2 = s[1] & s[2] & ~s[3]
Water Level Decoding: Level_Between_s2_s1 = s[1] & ~s[2]
Water Level Decoding: Level_Below_s1 = ~s[1]
fr1 = Level_Between_s3_s2 | Level_Between_s2_s1 | Level_Below_s1
fr2 = Level_Between_s2_s1 | Level_Below_s1
fr3 = Level_Below_s1
dfr = (Level_Between_s3_s2 & previous_state[0]) | (Level_Between_s2_s1 & (previous_state[0] | previous_state[1])) | (Level_Below_s1 & (previous_state[0] | previous_state[1] | previous_state[2]))
Outputs fr3, fr2, fr1, and dfr are updated on the rising edge of clk.
When reset is asserted high, fr3, fr2, fr1, and dfr are immediately asserted high on the next rising edge of clk.
The sensor inputs s[3:1] are sampled on the rising edge of clk.
The dfr output is asserted if the water level increases compared to the previous level, also on the rising edge of clk.
Registers are updated using non-blocking assignments.
Reset synchronously resets the registers to a specific state (all outputs high).
